channel.title: Cricket Score Counter — Learn Cricket
channel.description: Cricket scoring, laws, strategy and local cricket guides from Cricket Score Counter.

item.title: How to Read a Cricket Scorecard: Batting, Bowling and FoW
item.description: Learn to read any cricket scorecard: batting columns, dismissal notation, the extras line, fall of wickets and bowling figures like 4-0-28-2, with an example.

item.title: Ties, Super Overs and Bowl-Outs: Deciding Tied Matches
item.description: What counts as a tie, how a Super Over works under ICC playing conditions, what happens if the Super Over is tied, and fair tie-breakers for local cricket.

item.title: Bowling Tips for Beginners: Run-Up, Action and Length
item.description: Beginner bowling tips covering grip, a repeatable run-up, a legal and safe action, front-foot no-balls, and how to find a good line and length in matches.

item.title: Cricket Equipment Guide: Bat Sizes, Balls and Safety Gear
item.description: Cricket equipment for local players: bat size by height, English vs Kashmir willow, ball types and weights, and the safety gear hard-ball cricket needs.

item.title: Who Faces Next? Strike Rotation After Runs, Extras and Wickets
item.description: A scorer's guide to strike rotation: who is on strike after odd and even runs, overs, wides, no-balls, short runs and every kind of wicket, including catches.

item.title: Dead Ball, Short Runs and Penalty Runs Explained
item.description: When is the ball dead? What counts as a short run? Who gets five penalty runs and how are they scored? A practical guide to Laws 18, 20 and 41 for scorers.

item.title: Batting Tips for Beginners: Grip, Stance and Defence
item.description: Batting tips for new cricketers: how to grip the bat, set a balanced stance, play forward and back defence, leave the ball and rotate the strike in matches.

item.title: Overthrows in Cricket: How Boundary Overthrow Runs Count
item.description: How overthrows are scored: extra runs from a wild throw, the boundary overthrow rule, why crossing at the instant of the throw matters, plus local rules.

item.title: How to Pick Fair Teams for a Friendly Cricket Match
item.description: Practical methods for picking fair teams in friendly cricket: captain's draft, skill tiers, balancing bowlers and keepers, and setting a sensible batting order.

item.title: Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) Method Explained Simply
item.description: How the DLS method sets revised targets in rain-hit matches: resources, overs and wickets, par scores and why local cricket usually needs a simpler method.

item.title: Death Overs Bowling: Yorkers, Slower Balls and Fields
item.description: Death overs bowling tips for club cricketers: yorkers, slower balls, wide yorkers, field settings and over-by-over plans, with a worked final-overs example.

item.title: How to Record a Run Out: Runs, Batter Out and Who Faces
item.description: Scoring a run out properly: which runs count, how to tell which batter is out, who faces the next ball, and run outs off wides, no-balls and the last ball.

item.title: The Toss in Cricket: How It Works and Whether to Bat First
item.description: How the cricket toss works under the Laws, and how local captains should decide to bat or bowl first based on pitch, weather, light, team strength and format.

item.title: Umpire Signals Explained: Every Signal a Scorer Must Know
item.description: A scorer's guide to cricket umpire signals: four, six, wide, no-ball, bye, leg bye, dead ball, short run, penalty runs, revoke and more, with recording tips.

item.title: Powerplay Strategy for Batting and Bowling Sides
item.description: Powerplay rules for T20 and ODI cricket, how to scale them for local formats, and practical batting, bowling and field-setting plans for the opening overs.

item.title: Gully Cricket Rules and the House Rules Everyone Argues About
item.description: Gully and street cricket rules explained: one-tip-one-hand, last man batting, hitting into houses, trial balls, the one-pitch catch and how to settle disputes.

item.title: Byes vs Leg Byes: The Difference and How to Record Them
item.description: Byes and leg byes explained for scorers: when each applies, when leg byes are not allowed, why neither counts against the bowler, with worked examples.

item.title: Cricket Fielding Positions Explained: Slips to Long-On
item.description: Learn every cricket fielding position, from slips and gully to cover, mid-wicket and fine leg, plus the words that describe them and the leg-side rule.

item.title: Rain-Shortened Matches: Setting Fair Revised Targets
item.description: Simple, fair ways to set revised targets when rain shortens a local cricket match, with worked examples, honest weaknesses, and how DLS works in principle.

item.title: Tennis Ball and Tape Ball Cricket Rules Explained
item.description: Tennis ball and tape ball cricket rules: ball types, bowling actions, wides, no LBW, field restrictions and a sample 10-over rule sheet for weekend games.

item.title: Chasing a Target: Planning an Innings with Required Run Rate
item.description: How to use required run rate to plan a run chase: calculating it correctly, breaking the target into phases, and when to attack or consolidate in local cricket.

item.title: No-Balls and Free Hits: How to Score Them Correctly
item.description: How to score a no-ball and a free hit: the penalty run, runs off the bat, byes off a no-ball, which dismissals are allowed and common local scoring errors.

item.title: Box Cricket Rules: Pitch, Overs, Nets and Scoring
item.description: Common box cricket rules explained: team sizes, overs, pitch length, how runs are scored off the nets, dismissals and a ready-to-use 8-over rule sheet.

item.title: Which Dismissals Count for the Bowler? Wickets Explained
item.description: Bowled, caught, LBW, stumped and hit wicket go to the bowler. Run outs, timed out and obstruction do not. Here is how to credit every dismissal correctly.

item.title: Net Run Rate Explained with Worked Examples
item.description: Learn how net run rate is calculated, why an all-out team counts its full quota of overs, and how to convert 18.4 overs correctly, with worked examples.

item.title: How to Score a Wide: Runs, Dismissals and Local Rules
item.description: Learn exactly how to score a wide in cricket: the penalty run, runs taken off a wide, wides to the boundary, stumpings off a wide and common local rules.

item.title: How to Organise a Local Cricket Match: Complete Checklist
item.description: A practical checklist for organising a weekend local cricket match: booking the ground, confirming players, kit, rule sheets, timings and avoiding disputes.

item.title: The LBW Rule Explained Simply: Pitching, Impact and Shots
item.description: A plain-English guide to LBW under Law 36: where the ball pitched, where it hit the pad, whether a shot was offered, and how umpires decide without DRS.

item.title: Cricket Scoring Guide
item.description: A practical guide to cricket scoring, including legal balls, extras, wickets, strike rotation, targets, and local match scorekeeping tips.

item.title: Cricket Tournament Guide — Teams, Points Table & Player Stats
item.description: How to run a local cricket tournament — register teams, choose League or Knockout, and track an automatic points table and player leaderboard.

item.title: Cricket Statistics Explained — Batting, Bowling & Team Stats
item.description: Batting average, strike rate, economy rate, bowling average, run rate, and more explained.

item.title: Cricket Match Formats Explained
item.description: T20, 50-over, Test, box cricket, tennis ball, gully cricket, pairs cricket, and school formats explained.

item.title: Cricket Rules Guide for Local Matches
item.description: A complete cricket rules guide covering batting, bowling, fielding, extras, dismissals, innings structure, and local match variations.

item.title: Cricket Scorekeeping Tips
item.description: Practical cricket scorekeeping tips for local matches, including extras, wickets, over checks, strike rotation, and live score accuracy.
